To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Swedish-speaking children perceive their health to be better than Finnish-speaking children, but that this difference cannot be explained by socioeconomic factors, health behaviours or social relationships.

The perceived health of the Swedish speaking schoolchildren was better than that of their Finnish speaking peers, even after adjustment for a number of socioeconomic, social relationship and health behaviour variables.

the health advantage of the Swedish-speaking population of Finland could not be attributed, in the HBSC survey, to differences in socioeconomic background, social support, health behaviour, health complaints, or perceived health.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a minority group that has been shown to have a better health than that of the majority.
the health of the Finnish-speaking and Swedish-speaking populations in Finland.
the question of whether the health of Swedish-speaking schoolchildren is better than that for Finnish-speaking schoolchildren in the same social and economic circumstances.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the health of Swedish-speaking Finnish children is better than the health of their Finnish-speaking peers.
the health advantage of Swedish speakers is not attributable to socioeconomic factors, social relationships or lifestyle.
the health advantage of Swedish speakers is a fact but that the causes of the advantage are unknown.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Swedish-speaking children are healthier than Finnish-speaking children, but the reasons behind this are unknown.
the health advantage of the Swedish-speaking schoolchildren is not explained by the factors we studied.
the Swedish-speaking population of Finland has an advantage of perceived health, which cannot be explained by the known risk factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the health of Swedish-speaking schoolchildren is better than that among Finnish-speaking children in Finland, and the difference cannot be explained by known risk factors.
the better health of the Swedish minority cannot be attributed to socioeconomic status, health behaviour or social relationships.
the health advantage of the minority in Finland is not explained by socioeconomic factors or health behaviours, and that the reasons for the differences in perceived health remain to be identified.
